name: Michigan
overview: In Michigan, unpaid real property taxes are forfeited to the county treasurer in their second year of delinquency, and parcels still unpaid as of March 31 in the third year of delinquency are foreclosed. The foreclosing governmental unit then sells the foreclosed property at auction in a window that opens on the third Tuesday in July after the foreclosure judgment and closes on the first Tuesday in November. The minimum bid covers all delinquent taxes, interest, penalties and fees, and the state has a right of first refusal to buy foreclosed property before it goes to auction.

overview_sources.quote: Parcels are forfeited to the county treasurers when the real property taxes are in the second year of delinquency.
Real property taxes which remain unpaid as of March 31 in the third year of delinquency
beginning on the third Tuesday in July immediately succeeding the entry of the judgment under section 78k
ending on the immediately succeeding first Tuesday in November
The minimum bid must include all of the delinquent taxes, interest, penalties, and fees due on the property,
this state may exercise the right of first refusal to purchase foreclosed property

counties.how_to_bid: Register on the Zeus Auction site, then register for the Macomb County auction itself. Registration for each auction closes at 4:00 PM EST the day before the auction, and payment of the winning bid is due by 4:00 PM EST the day after. Properties are sold as is; the county's auction rules (subject to change) give the remaining terms. Deposit and minimum bid are not stated on the county page.
